name: Quito
tagline: Colonial Splendor at 9,000 Feet with Unbeatable Value
description: Quito sits in a dramatic Andean valley at 9,350 feet, offering spring-like weather year-round, a stunning UNESCO-listed colonial center, and some of the lowest costs of living in the Americas. Ecuador uses the US dollar (eliminating currency risk), offers affordable residency visas, and has a surprisingly robust healthcare system at a fraction of US costs. The Galapagos Islands, Amazon rainforest, and Pacific beaches are all accessible from this highland capital, making Quito an extraordinary base for adventurous FIRE retirees.

quickFacts.visa: 90-day visa-free for US citizens; Pensioner Visa with $1,375/month income requirement
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – improving; standard precautions in certain neighborhoods
quickFacts.climate: Spring-like year-round due to altitude; mild days and cool nights

housing.description: Modest studio/small 1BR in La Floresta (safe, walkable expat pocket)

dining.description: Cheap set-lunch almuerzos ($2.50–4) a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: IESS voluntary public affiliation. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more.

entertainment.description: Occasional cinema, free parks/museums, Pichincha hikes

1M.lifestyle: A modest studio or small one-bedroom in La Floresta, a safe, walkable pocket chosen deliberately over the cheapest citywide listings. Cheap set-lunch almuerzos a few times a week supplement mostly home cooking, and healthcare is IESS public affiliation. The Metro and buses cost cents a ride, and free parks, the colonial center, and hikes up Pichincha fill the weekends. The US dollar economy means no currency risk at all, and the budget leaves real margin — though the 9,350-foot altitude takes some adjustment.

housing.description: Nicer furnished 1BR in a safe pocket (La Floresta / La Carolina / Cumbayá edge)

dining.description: Dining out a few times a week at casual–mid restaurants

healthcare.description: Comprehensive local private insurance (Hospital Metropolitano access)

2M.lifestyle: A nicer furnished one-bedroom in a safe desirable pocket — La Floresta, La Carolina, or the Cumbayá edge — with dining out a few times a week at casual and mid-range spots. Comprehensive local private insurance brings access to hospitals like Metropolitano, and transport mixes Uber with the Metro. A gym, cinema, and occasional events fill the discretionary slack. The dollarized economy and dramatic Andean setting deliver strong value with room to spare.

housing.description: Top-of-local-market furnished 1BR on the González Suárez ridge (valley views) or luxury Cumbayá

3M.lifestyle: A top-of-local-market furnished one-bedroom on the González Suárez ridge with valley views, or a luxury unit in Cumbayá. Dining out is frequent, healthcare is a top local private plan with an international add-on, and transport is Uber-heavy with occasional domestic flights to the coast or Amazon. Concerts, nightlife, and weekend outings to cloud forests and hot springs are easily in budget. In a dollarized city this affordable, this is a comfortably affluent life with wide margin.

5M.lifestyle: A luxury penthouse or apartment in prime González Suárez or a resort-amenity home in Cumbayá, with a part-time housekeeper several days a week. Fine dining is regular, healthcare is a VIP private plan with an international network and medical evacuation, and a private car with a part-time driver handles transport. The discretionary budget covers clubs, wellness, frequent domestic travel, and international trips. Quito's low cost base means this level of comfort leaves generous margin.

10M.lifestyle: A best-address penthouse on the González Suárez ridge or a hacienda-style home in the Cumbayá valley, kept by full-time household staff. Dining is near-daily at the city's best tables, healthcare is an international concierge plan with worldwide coverage and evacuation, and a private driver and car are always on hand. The uncapped discretionary budget funds private Galápagos charters, luxury Amazon lodges, and first-class international travel. Quito's genuinely low cost ceiling means even this lavish life lands well below big-city FatFIRE — the surplus tends toward travel and Ecuador's conservation and arts causes.
